- `:752-753` `"settings.theme_update_success"` / `"settings.theme_update_error"`

---

## What adding a theme actually requires

Minimum viable path — **one new file, zero Go/config/template changes**:

1. Create `/Users/everick/Projects/CSCI435/gitea/web_src/css/themes/theme-<your-name>.css`. Filename must match `theme-*.css`; `InternalName` = filename minus `theme-` prefix and `.css` suffix.
2. Head it with a `gitea-theme-meta-info { --theme-display-name: "…"; --theme-color-scheme: "light"|"dark"|"auto"; }` block (last such block in the file wins).
3. Either `@import "./theme-gitea-dark.css";` and override a subset in `:root`, or define all ~295 `--color-*` vars plus `--is-dark-theme` and `color-scheme`.
4. Run `make vite` (or `make watch-frontend` in dev). Vite's glob picks it up; output lands at `public/assets/css/theme-<your-name>.<hash>.css` and gets registered in `public/assets/.vite/manifest.json`.
5. It appears in both the appearance page dropdown and the footer switcher automatically — **unless** `[ui].THEMES` is non-empty in `app.ini`, in which case add the internal name there.

Things to watch:
- The 1-second cache in `getAvailableThemes()` means changes show up quickly, but in `setting.IsProd` the theme list is loaded once and reused (`webtheme.go:227`), so a server restart is needed in production.
- If you add net-new `--color-*` variable names consumed elsewhere in `web_src/css`, add them to `theme-gitea-light.css` and `theme-gitea-dark.css` too, or `make lint-css` will fail via `csstools/value-no-unknown-custom-properties`.
- To make a theme the site default, set `[ui] DEFAULT_THEME` — an invalid value logs a startup problem at `webtheme.go:244-246`.
- For a pure runtime/no-rebuild option, drop the file at `custom/public/assets/css/theme-<name>.css` instead; `AssetFS`'s custom layer plus the `.css` fallback in `AssetURI` handle it.

**Issue #28 mentions colors, fonts, and "where features are located". How far should this implementation go?**

Options:
- **Color palettes only** - Add new color themes only. Gitea discovers theme CSS files automatically (vite globs web_src/css/themes/*.css, services/webtheme parses them), so this needs zero Go changes and is the cleanest reviewable diff.
- **Palettes + font choice** - Each theme also sets --fonts-proportional / --fonts-monospace. base.css defines both in :root and the theme stylesheet loads after index.css, so a theme can override them with no new plumbing.
- **Palettes + fonts + layout** - Also a compact/comfortable density option affecting spacing and where elements sit. This has no existing extension point — it means new CSS classes, a new user setting column, and Go/template changes. Much larger and riskier.

**Which palettes should the new themes use?**

Options:
- **Nord + Solarized + Gruvbox** - Three well-known developer palettes, each with light, dark, and auto variants = 9 new CSS files. Widely recognised, well-documented hex values, and each is visually distinct from stock Gitea.
- **Nord + Solarized** - Two palettes, 6 new CSS files. Smaller diff, faster to review and to get the color derivation right, still demonstrably "more than light/dark".
- **One palette first** - Ship Nord (light + dark + auto) as a proven pattern plus a short doc on adding more, then add others in follow-up PRs. Lowest risk, easiest review.

- **Swatch grid + live preview** - Replace the dropdown with a grid of preview cards on the appearance page that apply the theme live before saving. Largest frontend change: new template, new TS module, new CSS, and e2e coverage.

**There is NO shared base file between light and dark.** Each of the two full themes redeclares the complete variable set independently in its own `:root` block. The derivative themes (`-auto`, colorblind variants) are the only ones that use `@import`, e.g. `theme-gitea-auto.css` in full:

```css

@import "./theme-gitea-dark.css" (prefers-color-scheme: dark);

gitea-theme-meta-info {
  --theme-display-name: "Auto";
  --theme-color-scheme: "auto";
}
```

- **294 `--color-*` variables** in each of light and dark — the name sets are **byte-for-byte identical** (`diff` of the declared names between the two files is empty). So a new theme needs exactly those 294 names plus `--is-dark-theme`.

- Each `:root` also sets two *real* CSS properties, not custom properties: `accent-color: var(--color-accent)` and `color-scheme: light|dark`.

## 2. Variable derivation / generation

**There is no runtime or build-time color-scale generator.** No SCSS, no `generate-theme` script (`/Users/everick/Projects/CSCI435/gitea/build/` contains only Go generators plus `update-locales.sh`). Every one of the 294 colors is a hard-coded literal. The Sass `scale-color()` provenance survives only as comments.

What *does* consume the theme files programmatically:

- **`/Users/everick/Projects/CSCI435/gitea/tailwind.config.ts`** — reads both theme CSS files at config-load time with `postcss.parse`, collects every `:root` custom property, and maps the `color-*` ones into Tailwind's color palette:
  ```ts
  const vars = extractRootVars([
    readFileSync(new URL('web_src/css/themes/theme-gitea-light.css', import.meta.url), 'utf8'),
    readFileSync(new URL('web_src/css/themes/theme-gitea-dark.css', import.meta.url), 'utf8'),
  ].join('\n'));
  ...
  ...Object.fromEntries(vars.filter((prop) => prop.startsWith('color-')).map((prop) => {
    const color = prop.substring(6);
    return [color, `var(--color-${color})`];
  })),
  ```
  So `tw-bg-primary-light-3` works automatically. **A brand-new variable added to a theme file only becomes a Tailwind utility if it exists in the light or dark file specifically** — a third theme file is not scanned.

- **`/Users/everick/Projects/CSCI435/gitea/stylelint.config.ts` lines 4–8 and 111** — `csstools/value-no-unknown-custom-properties` with `importFrom: [base.css, theme-gitea-light.css, theme-gitea-dark.css]`. Using a `var(--color-foo)` that is not declared in one of those three files is a lint error.

- **`/Users/everick/Projects/CSCI435/gitea/vite.config.ts` lines 27–30, 274–275** — each theme file is its own build entry, so each produces a standalone hashed CSS bundle:
  ```ts
  const themes: Record<string, string> = {};
  for (const path of globSync('web_src/css/themes/*.css', {cwd: import.meta.dirname})) {
    themes[parse(path).name] = join(import.meta.dirname, path);
  }
  ```
  Drop a `theme-foo.css` into that directory and it is automatically an entry point (and automatically a selectable theme).

- **Backend discovery: `/Users/everick/Projects/CSCI435/gitea/services/webtheme/webtheme.go`** — scans for files matching `theme-*.css` (const `fileNamePrefix = "theme-"`, `fileNameSuffix = ".css"`) in `assets/css` (prod) or `web_src/css/themes` (vite dev mode), and regex-parses the `gitea-theme-meta-info { ... }` block out of the raw CSS to get display name / colorblind type / color scheme. The comment at lines 71–76 explains why it isn't `:root`:
  > *Not using ":root" because it is difficult to parse various ":root" blocks when importing other files, it is difficult to control the overriding, and it's difficult to avoid user's customized overridden styles.*

  Custom themes are dropped in `{CustomPath}/public/assets/css/theme-*.css` (documented in `custom/conf/app.example.ini` line 1380). `[ui].THEMES` whitelists, `[ui].DEFAULT_THEME` (default `gitea-auto`) picks the default — `custom/conf/app.example.ini` lines 1377–1381.

**CSS side:** only `--is-dark-theme: true|false` plus `color-scheme: dark|light`. The `<html data-theme="{{ctx.CurrentWebTheme.InternalName}}">` attribute in `/Users/everick/Projects/CSCI435/gitea/templates/base/head.tmpl` line 2 is informational — **no CSS rule selects on it** (the only `data-theme` selectors in CSS are tippy's unrelated tooltip variants in `web_src/css/modules/tippy.css`). **JS canonical reader — `/Users/everick/Projects/CSCI435/gitea/web_src/js/utils.ts` lines 39–42:**
```ts
export function isDarkTheme(): boolean {
  const style = window.getComputedStyle(document.documentElement);
  return style.getPropertyValue('--is-dark-theme').trim().toLowerCase() === 'true';
}
```

**The one attribute that CSS does branch on — `data-gitea-theme-dark`** — set as early as possible in `/Users/everick/Projects/CSCI435/gitea/web_src/js/webcomponents/index.ts` (the webcomponents bundle loads before the main bundle, to avoid flash):
```ts

  const sync = () => document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-gitea-theme-dark', String(isDarkTheme()));
  sync();
  window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').addEventListener('change', sync);  // for "auto" theme
}
```
Consumed in `/Users/everick/Projects/CSCI435/gitea/web_src/css/markup/content.css` lines 284–291 for GitHub's `#gh-dark-mode-only` / `#gh-light-mode-only` image fragments.

## Practical summary for authoring a new theme

Minimum viable new theme = one file `web_src/css/themes/theme-<name>.css` containing:
1. a `gitea-theme-meta-info { --theme-display-name: "..."; --theme-color-scheme: "light"|"dark"|"auto"; }` block (backend-parsed, must be a literal block — the parser takes the *last* occurrence of the identifier and only the *first* matched block),
2. a `:root` block with `--is-dark-theme`, all 294 `--color-*` names, plus `accent-color` and `color-scheme`.

Cheapest path: `@import "./theme-gitea-dark.css";` then override a subset in `:root` — exactly the pattern the four colorblind themes use. Caveats with that path: (a) Tailwind only scans the light and dark files, so any *new* variable name won't get a `tw-` utility; (b) stylelint's `importFrom` list likewise only knows base/light/dark; (c) the backend meta-info parser looks at the raw file text, so the meta block must be in your file, not only in the imported one.

```text
// Copyright 2024 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package webtheme

import (
	"io/fs"
	"net/url"
	"os"
	"path"
	"regexp"
	"sort"
	"strings"
	"sync/atomic"
	"time"

	"gitea.dev/modules/container"
	"gitea.dev/modules/log"
	"gitea.dev/modules/public"
	"gitea.dev/modules/setting"
	"gitea.dev/modules/util"
)

type themeCollectionStruct struct {
	lastCheckTime    time.Time
	usingViteDevMode bool

	themeList []*ThemeMetaInfo
	themeMap  map[string]*ThemeMetaInfo
}

var themeCollection atomic.Pointer[themeCollectionStruct]

const (
	fileNamePrefix = "theme-"
	fileNameSuffix = ".css"
)

type ThemeMetaInfo struct {
	FileName       string
	InternalName   string
	DisplayName    string
	ColorblindType string
	ColorScheme    string
}

func (info *ThemeMetaInfo) PublicAssetURI() string {
	return public.AssetURI("web_src/css/themes/theme-" + url.PathEscape(info.InternalName) + ".css")
}

func (info *ThemeMetaInfo) GetDescription() string {
	if info.ColorblindType == "red-green" {
		return "Red-green colorblind friendly"
	}
	if info.ColorblindType == "blue-yellow" {
		return "Blue-yellow colorblind friendly"
	}
	return ""
}

func (info *ThemeMetaInfo) GetExtraIconName() string {
	if info.ColorblindType == "red-green" {
		return "gitea-colorblind-redgreen"
	}
	if info.ColorblindType == "blue-yellow" {
		return "gitea-colorblind-blueyellow"
	}
	return ""
}

func parseThemeMetaInfoToMap(cssContent string) map[string]string {
	/*
		The theme meta info is stored in the CSS file's variables of `gitea-theme-meta-info` element,
		which is a privately defined and is only used by backend to extract the meta info.
		Not using ":root" because it is difficult to parse various ":root" blocks when importing other files,
		it is difficult to control the overriding, and it's difficult to avoid user's customized overridden styles.
	*/
	metaInfoContent := cssContent
	if pos := strings.LastIndex(metaInfoContent, "gitea-theme-meta-info"); pos >= 0 {
		metaInfoContent = metaInfoContent[pos:]
	}

	reMetaInfoItem := `
(
\s*(--[-\w]+)
\s*:
\s*(
("(\\"|[^"])*")
|('(\\'|[^'])*')
|([^'";]+)
)
\s*;?
\s*
)
`
	reMetaInfoItem = strings.ReplaceAll(reMetaInfoItem, "\n", "")
	reMetaInfoBlock := `\bgitea-theme-meta-info\s*\{(` + reMetaInfoItem + `+)\}`
	re := regexp.MustCompile(reMetaInfoBlock)
	matchedMetaInfoBlock := re.FindAllStringSubmatch(metaInfoContent, -1)
	if len(matchedMetaInfoBlock) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	re = regexp.MustCompile(strings.ReplaceAll(reMetaInfoItem, "\n", ""))
	matchedItems := re.FindAllStringSubmatch(matchedMetaInfoBlock[0][1], -1)
	m := map[string]string{}
	for _, item := range matchedItems {
		v := item[3]
		if after, ok := strings.CutPrefix(v, `"`); ok {
			v = strings.TrimSuffix(after, `"`)
			v = strings.ReplaceAll(v, `\"`, `"`)
		} else if after, ok := strings.CutPrefix(v, `'`); ok {
			v = strings.TrimSuffix(after, `'`)
			v = strings.ReplaceAll(v, `\'`, `'`)
		}
		m[item[2]] = v
	}
	return m
}

func defaultThemeMetaInfoByFileName(fileName string) *ThemeMetaInfo {
	internalName := strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimPrefix(fileName, fileNamePrefix), fileNameSuffix)
	// For built-in themes, the manifest knows the unhashed entry name (e.g. "theme-gitea-dark")
	// which lets us correctly strip the content hash without guessing.
	// Custom themes are not in the manifest and never have content hashes.
	if name := public.AssetNameFromHashedPath("css/" + fileName); name != "" {
		internalName = strings.TrimPrefix(name, fileNamePrefix)
	}
	themeInfo := &ThemeMetaInfo{
		FileName:     fileName,
		InternalName: internalName,
	}
	themeInfo.DisplayName = themeInfo.InternalName
	return themeInfo
}

func defaultThemeMetaInfoByInternalName(fileName string) *ThemeMetaInfo {
	return defaultThemeMetaInfoByFileName(fileNamePrefix + fileName + fileNameSuffix)
}

func parseThemeMetaInfo(fileName, cssContent string) *ThemeMetaInfo {
	themeInfo := defaultThemeMetaInfoByFileName(fileName)
	m := parseThemeMetaInfoToMap(cssContent)
	if m == nil {
		return themeInfo
	}
	themeInfo.DisplayName = m["--theme-display-name"]
	themeInfo.ColorblindType = m["--theme-colorblind-type"]
	themeInfo.ColorScheme = m["--theme-color-scheme"]
	return themeInfo
}

func collectThemeFiles(dirFS fs.ReadDirFS, fsPath string) (themes []*ThemeMetaInfo, _ error) {
	files, err := dirFS.ReadDir(fsPath)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	for _, file := range files {
		fileName := file.Name()
		if !strings.HasPrefix(fileName, fileNamePrefix) || !strings.HasSuffix(fileName, fileNameSuffix) {
			continue
		}
		content, err := fs.ReadFile(dirFS, path.Join(fsPath, file.Name()))
		if err != nil {
			log.Error("Failed to read theme file %q: %v", fileName, err)
			continue
		}
		themes = append(themes, parseThemeMetaInfo(fileName, util.UnsafeBytesToString(content)))
	}
	return themes, nil
}

func loadThemesFromAssets(isViteDevMode bool) (themeList []*ThemeMetaInfo, themeMap map[string]*ThemeMetaInfo) {
	var themeDir fs.ReadDirFS
	var themePath string

	if isViteDevMode {
		// In vite dev mode, Vite serves themes directly from source files.
		themeDir, themePath = os.DirFS(setting.StaticRootPath).(fs.ReadDirFS), "web_src/css/themes"
	} else {
		// Without vite dev server, use built assets from AssetFS.
		themeDir, themePath = public.AssetFS(), "assets/css"
	}

	foundThemes, err := collectThemeFiles(themeDir, themePath)
	if err != nil {
		log.Error("Failed to load theme files: %v", err)
		return themeList, themeMap
	}

	themeList = foundThemes
	if len(setting.UI.Themes) > 0 {
		themeList = nil // only allow the themes specified in the setting
		allowedThemes := container.SetOf(setting.UI.Themes...)
		for _, theme := range foundThemes {
			if allowedThemes.Contains(theme.InternalName) {
				themeList = append(themeList, theme)
			}
		}
	}

	sort.Slice(themeList, func(i, j int) bool {
		if themeList[i].InternalName == setting.UI.DefaultTheme {
			return true
		}
		if themeList[i].ColorblindType != themeList[j].ColorblindType {
			return themeList[i].ColorblindType < themeList[j].ColorblindType
		}
		return themeList[i].DisplayName < themeList[j].DisplayName
	})

	themeMap = map[string]*ThemeMetaInfo{}
	for _, theme := range themeList {
		themeMap[theme.InternalName] = theme
	}
	return themeList, themeMap
}

func getAvailableThemes() *themeCollectionStruct {
	themes := themeCollection.Load()

	now := time.Now()
	if themes != nil && now.Sub(themes.lastCheckTime) < time.Second {
		return themes
	}

	isViteDevMode := public.IsViteDevMode()
	useLoadedThemes := themes != nil && (setting.IsProd || themes.usingViteDevMode == isViteDevMode)
	if useLoadedThemes && len(themes.themeList) > 0 {
		return themes
	}

	themeList, themeMap := loadThemesFromAssets(isViteDevMode)
	hasAvailableThemes := len(themeList) > 0
	if !hasAvailableThemes {
		defaultTheme := defaultThemeMetaInfoByInternalName(setting.UI.DefaultTheme)
		themeList = []*ThemeMetaInfo{defaultTheme}
		themeMap = map[string]*ThemeMetaInfo{setting.UI.DefaultTheme: defaultTheme}
	}

	if setting.IsProd {
		if !hasAvailableThemes {
			setting.LogStartupProblem(1, log.ERROR, "No theme candidate in asset files, but Gitea requires there should be at least one usable theme")
		}
		if themeMap[setting.UI.DefaultTheme] == nil {
			setting.LogStartupProblem(1, log.ERROR, "Default theme %q is not available, please correct the '[ui].DEFAULT_THEME' setting in the config file", setting.UI.DefaultTheme)
		}
	}

	themes = &themeCollectionStruct{now, isViteDevMode, themeList, themeMap}
	themeCollection.Store(themes)
	return themes
}

func GetAvailableThemes() []*ThemeMetaInfo {
	return getAvailableThemes().themeList
}

func GetThemeMetaInfo(internalName string) *ThemeMetaInfo {
	return getAvailableThemes().themeMap[internalName]
}

// GuaranteeGetThemeMetaInfo guarantees to return a non-nil ThemeMetaInfo,
// to simplify the caller's logic, especially for templates.
// There are already enough warnings messages if the default theme is not available.
func GuaranteeGetThemeMetaInfo(internalName string) *ThemeMetaInfo {
	info := GetThemeMetaInfo(internalName)
	if info == nil {
		info = GetThemeMetaInfo(setting.UI.DefaultTheme)
	}
	if info == nil {
		info = &ThemeMetaInfo{DisplayName: "unavailable", InternalName: "unavailable", FileName: "unavailable"}
	}
	return info
}
```

	assert.Equal(t, map[string]string{
		"--k1": "v1",
		"--k2": `v"2`,
		"--k3": "v3",
		"--k4": "v'4",
		"--k5": "v5",
	}, m)

	// if an auto theme imports others, the meta info should be extracted from the last one
	// the meta in imported themes should be ignored to avoid incorrect overriding
	m = parseThemeMetaInfoToMap(`
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { gitea-theme-meta-info { --k1: foo; } }
@media (prefers-color-scheme: light) { gitea-theme-meta-info { --k1: bar; } }
gitea-theme-meta-info {
	--k2: real;
}`)
	assert.Equal(t, map[string]string{"--k2": "real"}, m)

	// compressed CSS, no trailing semicolon
	m = parseThemeMetaInfoToMap(`gitea-theme-meta-info{--k1:"v1"}`)
	assert.Equal(t, map[string]string{"--k1": "v1"}, m)
	m = parseThemeMetaInfoToMap(`gitea-theme-meta-info{--k1:"v1";--k2:"v2"}`)
	assert.Equal(t, map[string]string{"--k1": "v1", "--k2": "v2"}, m)
}
```
</details></tool-use>

```markdown
# Add selectable color palettes (issue #28)

## Context

Issue [#28](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/28) ("UI Views, Color Pallets") asks for
presets a user can pick from in settings, so the site is not limited to one light and one dark
option. Today this fork ships exactly one palette — Gitea blue-and-grey — in `Light`, `Dark` and
`Auto` flavours, plus four colorblind-adjusted variants of that same palette.

This change adds **four new palettes — Nord, Solarized, Gruvbox and Catppuccin** — each in light,
dark and auto flavours. A user picks one from Settings → Appearance, or from the footer switcher;
the choice already persists to `user.theme` for signed-in users and to the `gitea_theme` cookie for
anonymous ones.

Scope agreed with the requester: **colors only.** No font switching, no layout/density option, and
no change to the theme picker UI. Those were considered and deliberately left out — a density
option in particular has no existing extension point and would need a new user column, a migration
and template changes.

## Why this is cheap

Gitea's theme system is already fully data-driven, so this is a CSS-only change:

- `vite.config.ts` globs `web_src/css/themes/*.css` and makes each file its own build entry, so a
  new file is picked up with no build-config change.
- `services/webtheme/webtheme.go` discovers themes by scanning for `theme-*.css` and regex-parsing
  a `gitea-theme-meta-info { ... }` block out of each. `InternalName` is the filename minus the
  `theme-` prefix and `.css` suffix.
- `routers/web/user/setting/profile.go` → `Appearance` passes `webtheme.GetAvailableThemes()`
  straight to the template; `templates/user/settings/appearance.tmpl` ranges over it.
  `routers/web/misc/webtheme.go` does the same for the footer switcher.

**No Go, template, locale or config changes are required.**

15. **`./.claude-students/check.sh` passes before you push [checked].** It is dependency-free and
    finishes in under a second.

## The guide layer (rules 16-22)

`guide/` holds a plain-English page for each reference page in `docs/`, same filename. It exists so
a person new to Go and to this codebase can get oriented. It is **derived**, not independent.

16. Every guide carries `source:`, `source-hash:` and `verified-at:` in its frontmatter **[checked]**.
17. A guide's `source:` names a real `docs/*.md` with the **same filename** **[checked]**.
18. `source-hash:` is the first 16 characters of `sha256sum docs/<name>.md`. If the reference page
    changes and the guide is not regenerated, `check.sh` reports **drift** **[checked]**. Regenerating
    means: reread the reference page, rewrite the guide, update the hash and `verified-at`.
19. Guide headings match `guide/_TEMPLATE.md` exactly and in order **[checked]**.
20. Guides are capped at **200 lines**, code fences at **30** **[checked]** — teaching needs more room
    than reference does.
21. **A guide adds explanation, vocabulary and worked steps. It adds no new facts.** Every repo path
    a guide cites must also be cited by its source page **[checked]**. If you need a fact the
    reference page lacks, add it *there* first, which bumps the hash and forces the guide to be
    regenerated in the same commit — exactly the intended order.
22. `guide/START-HERE.md` has no source page. It is exempt from rules 17, 18 and 21, and is where
    cross-cutting material lives that no single reference page owns.

**Never fix a fact in `guide/`.** If the two layers disagree, the reference page is the truth and
the guide is stale: fix `docs/`, regenerate the guide, ship both in one PR. A disagreement is a bug
report against `docs/`, not an editing job in `guide/`.

**Known limitation:** a hand-edit to a guide that only rewords prose is not mechanically
detectable. Rule 21 catches invented facts; rule 18 catches a stale guide; review catches the rest.

## Updating `verified-at`

`verified-at` is the short SHA the doc was last checked against, from `git rev-parse --short HEAD`.
Bump it whenever you confirm or correct a doc. A doc whose `verified-at` is far behind `main` has
not been checked recently — treat its details as hints and confirm them in the code before relying
on them.

function h2r(h){h=h.replace("#","");return [parseInt(h.slice(0,2),16),parseInt(h.slice(2,4),16),parseInt(h.slice(4,6),16)];}
function rgb2hsl(r,g,b){r/=255;g/=255;b/=255;const mx=Math.max(r,g,b),mn=Math.min(r,g,b);let h=0,s=0;const l=(mx+mn)/2;const d=mx-mn;if(d){s=l>0.5?d/(2-mx-mn):d/(mx+mn);switch(mx){case r:h=((g-b)/d+(g<b?6:0));break;case g:h=((b-r)/d+2);break;default:h=((r-g)/d+4);}h*=60;}return [h,s,l];}

console.log("=== primary dark-N (light theme) ===");
[...light].forEach((c,i)=>{const [h,s,l]=rgb2hsl(...h2r(c));console.log((i===0?"base":"dark-"+i).padEnd(7),c,"H="+h.toFixed(1),"S="+s.toFixed(4),"L="+l.toFixed(4));});
console.log("=== primary light-N ===");
lightL.forEach((c,i)=>{const [h,s,l]=rgb2hsl(...h2r(c));console.log(("light-"+(i+1)).padEnd(7),c,"H="+h.toFixed(1),"S="+s.toFixed(4),"L="+l.toFixed(4));});
'

const secL={base:"#d0d7de",d1:"#c7ced5",d2:"#b9c0c7",d3:"#99a0a7",d4:"#899097",d5:"#7a8188",d6:"#6a7178",d7:"#5b6269",d8:"#4b5259",d9:"#3c434a",d10:"#2c333a",d11:"#1d242b",d12:"#0d141b",d13:"#00040b",l1:"#dee5ec",l2:"#e4ebf2",l3:"#ebf2f9",l4:"#f1f8ff"};
console.log("=== secondary (light theme) ===");
for(const [k,c] of Object.entries(secL)){const [h,s,l]=rgb2hsl(...h2r(c));console.log(k.padEnd(5),c,"H="+h.toFixed(1),"S="+s.toFixed(4),"L="+l.toFixed(4));}
const secD={base:"#3f4248",d1:"#46494f",d2:"#4f5259",d3:"#5e626a",d4:"#6f747d",d5:"#7d828c",d6:"#8b8f98",d7:"#999da4",d8:"#a8abb1",d9:"#aeb1b8",d10:"#bbbec3",d11:"#c8cacf",d12:"#d2d4d7",d13:"#d5d6d9",l1:"#35373c",l2:"#2c2e32",l3:"#1f2124",l4:"#191a1c"};

import {colord} from 'colord';
import type {AnyColor} from 'colord';

/** Returns relative luminance for a SRGB color - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Relative_luminance */
// Keep this in sync with modules/util/color.go
function getRelativeLuminance(color: AnyColor): number {
  const {r, g, b} = colord(color).toRgb();
  return (0.2126729 * r + 0.7151522 * g + 0.072175 * b) / 255;
}

function useLightText(backgroundColor: AnyColor): boolean {
  return getRelativeLuminance(backgroundColor) < 0.453;
}

/** Given a background color, returns a black or white foreground color with the highest contrast ratio. */
// In the future, the APCA contrast function, or CSS `contrast-color` will be better.
// https://github.com/color-js/color.js/blob/eb7b53f7a13bb716ec8b28c7a56f052cd599acd9/src/contrast/APCA.js#L42
export function contrastColor(backgroundColor: AnyColor): string {
  return useLightText(backgroundColor) ? '#fff' : '#000';
}

function resolveColors(obj: Record<string, string>): Record<string, string> {
  const styles = window.getComputedStyle(document.documentElement);
  const getColor = (name: string) => styles.getPropertyValue(name).trim();
  return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(obj).map(([key, value]) => [key, getColor(value)]));
}

export const chartJsColors = resolveColors({
  text: '--color-text',
  border: '--color-secondary-alpha-60',
  commits: '--color-primary-alpha-60',
  additions: '--color-green',
  deletions: '--color-red',
});

function extractRootVars(css: string) {
  const root = parse(css);
  const vars = new Set<string>();
  root.walkRules((rule) => {
    if (rule.selector !== ':root') return;
    rule.each((node) => {
      if (node.type === 'decl' && node.value && node.prop.startsWith('--')) {
        vars.add(node.prop.substring(2));
      }
    });
  });
  return Array.from(vars);
}

````markdown
# Add selectable color palettes (issue #28)

## Context

Issue [#28](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/28) ("UI Views, Color Pallets") asks for
presets a user can pick in settings, so the site is not limited to one light and one dark option.
Today this fork ships exactly one palette — Gitea blue-and-grey — in `Light`, `Dark` and `Auto`
flavours, plus four colorblind-adjusted variants of that same palette.

This change adds **four new palettes — Nord, Solarized, Gruvbox and Catppuccin** — each in light,
dark and auto flavours. Users pick one from Settings → Appearance or the footer switcher; the
choice already persists to `user.theme` for signed-in users and the `gitea_theme` cookie for
anonymous ones.

**Scope: colors only.** No font switching, no layout/density option, no change to the picker UI.
A density option in particular has no existing extension point — it would need a new user column, a
migration and template changes — and was deliberately left out.

## Why this is a CSS-only change

Gitea's theme system is already fully data-driven:

- `vite.config.ts` globs `web_src/css/themes/*.css` and makes each file its own build entry, so a
  new file needs no build-config change. Output lands at
  `public/assets/css/theme-<name>.<hash>.css`.
- `services/webtheme/webtheme.go` discovers themes by scanning for `theme-*.css` and regex-parsing
  a `gitea-theme-meta-info { ... }` block out of each. `InternalName` is the filename minus the
  `theme-` prefix and `.css` suffix.
- `routers/web/user/setting/profile.go` → `Appearance` hands `webtheme.GetAvailableThemes()`
  straight to `templates/user/settings/appearance.tmpl`; `routers/web/misc/webtheme.go` does the
  same for the footer switcher.
- `templates/base/head_style.tmpl` emits the theme `<link>` **after** `index.css`, so a theme's
  `:root` block wins over `base.css`.

**No Go, template, locale or `app.ini` changes are required.** `[ui].THEMES` is empty by default,
which means "allow everything found".

## Approach

### 1. Follow the existing variant pattern

The four colorblind themes already establish the cheap pattern: `@import` the matching stock base,
declare your own meta block, then override a subset in `:root`. Each new theme does the same, so
the diff shows only what the palette actually changes and future upstream variable additions are
inherited for free.

Light and dark files look like:

```css
@import "./theme-gitea-light.css";

gitea-theme-meta-info {
  --theme-display-name: "Nord Light";
  --theme-color-scheme: "light";
}

/* Nord palette - https://www.nordtheme.com/docs/colors-and-palettes */
:root {
  --color-primary: #5e81ac;
  /* ... */
}
```

Auto files are 8 lines, mirroring `theme-gitea-auto.css`:

```css
@import "./theme-nord-light.css" (prefers-color-scheme: light);
@import "./theme-nord-dark.css" (prefers-color-scheme: dark);

gitea-theme-meta-info {
  --theme-display-name: "Nord Auto";
  --theme-color-scheme: "auto";
}
```

Import the **matching** stock base (light theme imports `theme-gitea-light.css`), never a single
one for both — light and dark differ in more than colors. `theme-gitea-dark.css` also carries emoji
invert rules and a different `--color-editor-line-highlight` / `--color-project-column-bg`
derivation, and it sets `color-scheme: dark`, `accent-color` and `--is-dark-theme: true`. All of
that is inherited; **do not re-declare `--is-dark-theme` or `color-scheme`** — the colorblind
variants do not either.

### 2. Which of the 294 variables to override

Read `web_src/css/themes/theme-gitea-light.css` for the canonical order and keep the same order and
grouping in each new file, so a reviewer can diff them side by side.

**Override (~150 declarations per light/dark file):**

| Group | Variables |
| --- | --- |
| Primary ramp (33) | `--color-primary`, `-contrast`, `-dark-1..7`, `-light-1..7`, `-alpha-10..90`, `-hover`, `-active` |
| Secondary ramp (36) | `--color-secondary`, `-dark-1..13`, `-light-1..4`, `-alpha-10..90`, `-button`, `-hover`, `-active` |
| Surfaces (~22) | `--color-body`, `-box-header`, `-box-body`, `-box-body-highlight`, `-menu`, `-card`, `-button`, `-code-bg`, `-secondary-bg`, `-nav-bg`, `-secondary-nav-bg`, `-input-background`, `-input-toggle-background`, `-expand-button`, `-timeline`, `-markup-table-row`, `-markup-code-block`, `-markup-code-inline`, `-hover-opaque`, `-shadow-opaque`, `-tooltip-bg`, `-tooltip-text` |
| Text (6) | `--color-text-dark`, `-text`, `-text-light`, `-text-light-1..3` |
| Neutral overlays (~7) | `--color-light`, `-light-border`, `-hover`, `-active`, `-shadow`, `-reaction-bg`, `-overlay-backdrop` |
| Labels + misc (~6) | `--color-label-bg`, `-label-hover-bg`, `-label-active-bg`, `--color-highlight-fg`, `-highlight-bg`, `--color-workflow-edge-hover` |
| Diff (13) | `--color-diff-{added,removed}-{fg,linenum-bg,row-bg,row-border,word-bg}`, `--color-diff-moved-row-bg/-border`, `--color-diff-inactive` |
| Syntax (41) | all `--color-syntax-*` |

Diff and syntax are the highest-impact groups on a code host and all four palettes publish
canonical syntax mappings, so these are mostly transcription rather than invention.

**Leave inherited** — overriding these buys little and risks breaking meaning:

- Named hues (`--color-red`, `--color-green`, … × 4 variants, 48 vars) — these back user-chosen
  label colors and must stay recognisable.
- Badges (12), ANSI (16), `--color-series-16-0..15` (git graph lanes, identical in both stock
  themes), semantic status (17), console (9), `--color-git`, `--color-logo`.

Many variables resolve through `var()` and so update for free once the ramps are overridden:
`--color-accent`, `--color-small-accent`, `--color-project-column-bg`, `--color-reaction-hover-bg`,
`--color-reaction-active-bg`, `--color-nav-hover-bg`, `--color-input-border`,
`--color-editor-selection`, `--color-editor-line-highlight`, `--color-placeholder-text`,
`--color-caret`, `--color-footer`, `--color-danger`, `--color-input-text`, `--color-nav-text`,
`--color-label-text`. Do not re-declare them.

**Do not introduce any new `--color-*` name.** `tailwind.config.ts` and `stylelint.config.ts` read
only `base.css`, `theme-gitea-light.css` and `theme-gitea-dark.css`; a name that exists nowhere in
those three fails `csstools/value-no-unknown-custom-properties` and gets no `tw-` utility.

### 3. Generating the ramps

The repo has **no color-scale generator** — every stock value is a hard-coded literal (the
`scale-color()` provenance survives only in comments; Sass is long gone). So generate once and
paste literals.

Write a throwaway script under the scratchpad — **not committed** — using `colord`, which is
already a dependency (`package.json`), run with plain `node` (v26 strips TS types natively).

The ramp convention, measured from stock `--color-primary: #4183c4` (HSL L ≈ 0.512):

- `dark-1..4` / `light-1..4` are roughly **±5% absolute HSL lightness steps** from the base.
- `dark-5,6,7` land near L ≈ 0.206 / 0.102 / 0.031; `light-5,6,7` near L ≈ 0.804 / 0.902 / 0.971 —
  i.e. the tail interpolates toward black/white rather than continuing the 5% step.
- `alpha-10..90` are simply the base hex plus an alpha byte:
  `19 33 4b 66 80 99 b3 cc e1`.
- **The dark theme inverts the ramps.** In `theme-gitea-dark.css`, `--color-primary-dark-1` holds
  the *lighter* value (`#548fca`, which is light's `light-1`) and `light-1` holds the darker one,
  with `--color-primary-hover: var(--color-primary-light-1)` and `-active:
  var(--color-primary-light-2)`. Same inversion for the secondary ramp. Generate one lighter ramp
  and one darker ramp, then assign them to `dark-N`/`light-N` per theme direction.
- Clamp at the ends: a base that is already very light or very dark (Gruvbox yellow `#d79921`,
  Solarized base03 `#002b36`) must target the absolute lightness anchors above rather than stepping
  blindly, or the last two or three stops collapse into the same color.
- Emit **lowercase** hex — `stylelint.config.ts` sets `@stylistic/color-hex-case: 'lower'`.

### 4. Naming

Uniform across all four palettes, so filename, internal name and display name line up:

| Files | InternalName | DisplayName | ColorScheme |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `theme-nord-light.css` | `nord-light` | `Nord Light` | `light` |
| `theme-nord-dark.css` | `nord-dark` | `Nord Dark` | `dark` |
| `theme-nord-auto.css` | `nord-auto` | `Nord Auto` | `auto` |

…and the same for `solarized`, `gruvbox`, `catppuccin`. For Catppuccin use the Latte flavour for
light and Mocha for dark, noted in a CSS comment rather than in the display name.

Known cosmetic consequence: `loadThemesFromAssets` sorts the default theme first, then by
`ColorblindType`, then by `DisplayName`. All new themes have an empty `ColorblindType`, so they
sort alphabetically alongside the stock `Auto` / `Dark` / `Light`. Each palette's three entries stay
adjacent; the stock three end up scattered among them. Acceptable — grouping by palette family
would mean a new meta key and a Go change, which is out of the agreed scope.

### 5. Test

Add `web_src/css/themes/themes.test.ts`, picked up by vitest's `web_src/**/*.test.ts` include
(`vitest.config.ts`). A `.ts` file in that directory does not affect vite's `*.css` theme glob.
Read the theme files with `node:fs` and assert, for **every** file in the directory:

1. It contains a `gitea-theme-meta-info` block with a non-empty `--theme-display-name` and a
   `--theme-color-scheme` of `light` | `dark` | `auto`.
2. Display names are unique across themes.
3. Each non-auto file transitively resolves `--is-dark-theme` consistently with its declared
   `--theme-color-scheme`, and each auto file imports exactly one light and one dark file under the
   matching `prefers-color-scheme` condition.
4. Contrast: resolve each theme's `:root` (following the single `@import` into the stock base, and
   one level of `var()` indirection) and assert WCAG ratios with `colord`'s a11y plugin —
   `--color-text` on `--color-body`, `--color-box-body`, `--color-menu` and `--color-card` at
   ≥ 4.5:1; `--color-text-light-1/-2` on `--color-body` at ≥ 4.5:1; `--color-primary-contrast` on
   `--color-primary` at ≥ 4.5:1; `--color-primary` on `--color-body` at ≥ 3:1.

Run the contrast assertions against the **stock themes first** and set thresholds to what stock
already passes. If a stock pair fails, exclude that specific pair with a comment naming it — do not
retune upstream colors to make a new test go green.

This covers issue #28's regression surface far better than an e2e test would, and matches
`AGENTS.md`'s preference for unit tests. `tests/integration/user_settings_test.go` already GETs
`/user/settings/appearance`, so the page itself stays covered.

Per `.claude-students/MAINTENANCE.md` rule 13, land doc updates in the same PR. Add an **"Add a
colour theme"** recipe to `.claude-students/docs/frontend-css.md` (currently 83 lines, cap 120)
covering: the `theme-*.css` filename contract, the required `gitea-theme-meta-info` block, the
`@import`-the-matching-base pattern, and the rule that new variable names must also exist in
`theme-gitea-light.css` / `theme-gitea-dark.css` or lint fails.

Rule 18 then requires regenerating `.claude-students/guide/frontend-css.md`: reread the reference
page, rewrite the guide, and update its `source-hash` (first 16 chars of `sha256sum`) and
`verified-at`. Both files ship in the same commit. Run `./.claude-students/check.sh` before pushing.

## Approved Plan:
# Add selectable color palettes (issue #28)

## Context

Issue [#28](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/28) ("UI Views, Color Pallets") asks for
presets a user can pick in settings, so the site is not limited to one light and one dark option.
Today this fork ships exactly one palette — Gitea blue-and-grey — in `Light`, `Dark` and `Auto`
flavours, plus four colorblind-adjusted variants of that same palette.

This change adds **four new palettes — Nord, Solarized, Gruvbox and Catppuccin** — each in light,
dark and auto flavours. Users pick one from Settings → Appearance or the footer switcher; the
choice already persists to `user.theme` for signed-in users and the `gitea_theme` cookie for
anonymous ones.

**Scope: colors only.** No font switching, no layout/density option, no change to the picker UI.
A density option in particular has no existing extension point — it would need a new user column, a
migration and template changes — and was deliberately left out.

## Why this is a CSS-only change

Gitea's theme system is already fully data-driven:

- `vite.config.ts` globs `web_src/css/themes/*.css` and makes each file its own build entry, so a
  new file needs no build-config change. Output lands at
  `public/assets/css/theme-<name>.<hash>.css`.
- `services/webtheme/webtheme.go` discovers themes by scanning for `theme-*.css` and regex-parsing
  a `gitea-theme-meta-info { ... }` block out of each. `InternalName` is the filename minus the
  `theme-` prefix and `.css` suffix.
- `routers/web/user/setting/profile.go` → `Appearance` hands `webtheme.GetAvailableThemes()`
  straight to `templates/user/settings/appearance.tmpl`; `routers/web/misc/webtheme.go` does the
  same for the footer switcher.
- `templates/base/head_style.tmpl` emits the theme `<link>` **after** `index.css`, so a theme's
  `:root` block wins over `base.css`.

**No Go, template, locale or `app.ini` changes are required.** `[ui].THEMES` is empty by default,
which means "allow everything found".

## Approach

### 1. Follow the existing variant pattern

The four colorblind themes already establish the cheap pattern: `@import` the matching stock base,
declare your own meta block, then override a subset in `:root`. Each new theme does the same, so
the diff shows only what the palette actually changes and future upstream variable additions are
inherited for free.

Light and dark files look like:

```css
@import "./theme-gitea-light.css";

gitea-theme-meta-info {
  --theme-display-name: "Nord Light";
  --theme-color-scheme: "light";
}

/* Nord palette - https://www.nordtheme.com/docs/colors-and-palettes */
:root {
  --color-primary: #5e81ac;
  /* ... */
}
```

Auto files are 8 lines, mirroring `theme-gitea-auto.css`:

```css
@import "./theme-nord-light.css" (prefers-color-scheme: light);
@import "./theme-nord-dark.css" (prefers-color-scheme: dark);

gitea-theme-meta-info {
  --theme-display-name: "Nord Auto";
  --theme-color-scheme: "auto";
}
```

Import the **matching** stock base (light theme imports `theme-gitea-light.css`), never a single
one for both — light and dark differ in more than colors. `theme-gitea-dark.css` also carries emoji
invert rules and a different `--color-editor-line-highlight` / `--color-project-column-bg`
derivation, and it sets `color-scheme: dark`, `accent-color` and `--is-dark-theme: true`. All of
that is inherited; **do not re-declare `--is-dark-theme` or `color-scheme`** — the colorblind
variants do not either.

### 2. Which of the 294 variables to override

Read `web_src/css/themes/theme-gitea-light.css` for the canonical order and keep the same order and
grouping in each new file, so a reviewer can diff them side by side.

**Override (~150 declarations per light/dark file):**

| Group | Variables |
| --- | --- |
| Primary ramp (25) | `--color-primary`, `-contrast`, `-dark-1..7`, `-light-1..7`, `-alpha-10..90` |
| Secondary ramp (27) | `--color-secondary`, `-dark-1..13`, `-light-1..4`, `-alpha-10..90` |
| Surfaces (~22) | `--color-body`, `-box-header`, `-box-body`, `-box-body-highlight`, `-menu`, `-card`, `-button`, `-code-bg`, `-secondary-bg`, `-nav-bg`, `-secondary-nav-bg`, `-input-background`, `-input-toggle-background`, `-expand-button`, `-timeline`, `-markup-table-row`, `-markup-code-block`, `-markup-code-inline`, `-hover-opaque`, `-shadow-opaque`, `-tooltip-bg`, `-tooltip-text` |
| Text (6) | `--color-text-dark`, `-text`, `-text-light`, `-text-light-1..3` |
| Neutral overlays (~7) | `--color-light`, `-light-border`, `-hover`, `-active`, `-shadow`, `-reaction-bg`, `-overlay-backdrop` |
| Labels + misc (~6) | `--color-label-bg`, `-label-hover-bg`, `-label-active-bg`, `--color-highlight-fg`, `-highlight-bg`, `--color-workflow-edge-hover` |
| Diff (13) | `--color-diff-{added,removed}-{fg,linenum-bg,row-bg,row-border,word-bg}`, `--color-diff-moved-row-bg/-border`, `--color-diff-inactive` |
| Syntax (41) | all `--color-syntax-*` |

Diff and syntax are the highest-impact groups on a code host and all four palettes publish
canonical syntax mappings, so these are mostly transcription rather than invention.

**Leave inherited** — overriding these buys little and risks breaking meaning:

- Named hues (`--color-red`, `--color-green`, … × 4 variants, 48 vars) — these back user-chosen
  label colors and must stay recognisable.
- Badges (12), ANSI (16), `--color-series-16-0..15` (git graph lanes, identical in both stock
  themes), semantic status (17), console (9), `--color-git`, `--color-logo`.

Many variables resolve through `var()` and so update for free once the ramps are overridden:
`--color-accent`, `--color-small-accent`, `--color-project-column-bg`, `--color-reaction-hover-bg`,
`--color-reaction-active-bg`, `--color-nav-hover-bg`, `--color-input-border`,
`--color-editor-selection`, `--color-editor-line-highlight`, `--color-placeholder-text`,
`--color-caret`, `--color-footer`, `--color-danger`, `--color-input-text`, `--color-nav-text`,
`--color-label-text`. Do not re-declare them.

The ramp tails are `var()` refs too and must also be left alone: `--color-primary-hover` /
`-active` and `--color-secondary-button` / `-hover` / `-active` point at `dark-N` in the light
theme and `light-N` in the dark theme. Importing the matching base gives each file the right
reference automatically; re-declaring them would silently undo the inversion.

**Do not introduce any new `--color-*` name.** `tailwind.config.ts` and `stylelint.config.ts` read
only `base.css`, `theme-gitea-light.css` and `theme-gitea-dark.css`; a name that exists nowhere in
those three fails `csstools/value-no-unknown-custom-properties` and gets no `tw-` utility.

### 3. Generating the ramps

The repo has **no color-scale generator** — every stock value is a hard-coded literal (the
`scale-color()` provenance survives only in comments; Sass is long gone). So generate once and
paste literals.

Write a throwaway script under the scratchpad — **not committed** — using `colord`, which is
already a dependency (`package.json`), run with plain `node` (v26 strips TS types natively).

The ramp convention, measured from stock `--color-primary: #4183c4` (HSL L ≈ 0.512):

- `dark-1..4` / `light-1..4` are roughly **±5% absolute HSL lightness steps** from the base.
- `dark-5,6,7` land near L ≈ 0.206 / 0.102 / 0.031; `light-5,6,7` near L ≈ 0.804 / 0.902 / 0.971 —
  i.e. the tail interpolates toward black/white rather than continuing the 5% step.
- `alpha-10..90` are simply the base hex plus an alpha byte:
  `19 33 4b 66 80 99 b3 cc e1`.
- **The dark theme inverts the ramps.** In `theme-gitea-dark.css`, `--color-primary-dark-1` holds
  the *lighter* value (`#548fca`, which is light's `light-1`) and `light-1` holds the darker one,
  with `--color-primary-hover: var(--color-primary-light-1)` and `-active:
  var(--color-primary-light-2)`. Same inversion for the secondary ramp. Generate one lighter ramp
  and one darker ramp, then assign them to `dark-N`/`light-N` per theme direction.
- Clamp at the ends: a base that is already very light or very dark (Gruvbox yellow `#d79921`,
  Solarized base03 `#002b36`) must target the absolute lightness anchors above rather than stepping
  blindly, or the last two or three stops collapse into the same color.
- Emit **lowercase** hex — `stylelint.config.ts` sets `@stylistic/color-hex-case: 'lower'`.

### 4. Naming

Uniform across all four palettes, so filename, internal name and display name line up:

| Files | InternalName | DisplayName | ColorScheme |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `theme-nord-light.css` | `nord-light` | `Nord Light` | `light` |
| `theme-nord-dark.css` | `nord-dark` | `Nord Dark` | `dark` |
| `theme-nord-auto.css` | `nord-auto` | `Nord Auto` | `auto` |

…and the same for `solarized`, `gruvbox`, `catppuccin`. For Catppuccin use the Latte flavour for
light and Mocha for dark, noted in a CSS comment rather than in the display name.

Known cosmetic consequence: `loadThemesFromAssets` sorts the default theme first, then by
`ColorblindType`, then by `DisplayName`. All new themes have an empty `ColorblindType`, so they
sort alphabetically alongside the stock `Auto` / `Dark` / `Light`. Each palette's three entries stay
adjacent; the stock three end up scattered among them. Acceptable — grouping by palette family
would mean a new meta key and a Go change, which is out of the agreed scope.

### 5. Test

Add `web_src/css/themes/themes.test.ts`, picked up by vitest's `web_src/**/*.test.ts` include
(`vitest.config.ts`). A `.ts` file in that directory does not affect vite's `*.css` theme glob.
Read the theme files with `node:fs` and assert, for **every** file in the directory:

1. It contains a `gitea-theme-meta-info` block with a non-empty `--theme-display-name` and a
   `--theme-color-scheme` of `light` | `dark` | `auto`.
2. Display names are unique across themes.
3. Each non-auto file transitively resolves `--is-dark-theme` consistently with its declared
   `--theme-color-scheme`, and each auto file imports exactly one light and one dark file under the
   matching `prefers-color-scheme` condition.
4. Contrast: resolve each theme's `:root` (following the single `@import` into the stock base, and
   one level of `var()` indirection) and assert WCAG ratios with `colord`'s a11y plugin —
   `--color-text` on `--color-body`, `--color-box-body`, `--color-menu` and `--color-card` at
   ≥ 4.5:1; `--color-text-light-1/-2` on `--color-body` at ≥ 4.5:1; `--color-primary-contrast` on
   `--color-primary` at ≥ 4.5:1; `--color-primary` on `--color-body` at ≥ 3:1.

Run the contrast assertions against the **stock themes first** and set thresholds to what stock
already passes. If a stock pair fails, exclude that specific pair with a comment naming it — do not
retune upstream colors to make a new test go green.

This covers issue #28's regression surface far better than an e2e test would, and matches
`AGENTS.md`'s preference for unit tests. `tests/integration/user_settings_test.go` already GETs
`/user/settings/appearance`, so the page itself stays covered.

func entryStyleURLs(jsEntrySrc, devStylesheetSrc string) []string {
	if IsViteDevMode() {
		return []string{devAssetURL(devStylesheetSrc)}
	}
	entries := getManifestData().entries
	var urls []string
	seen := make(map[string]bool)
	var walk func(key string)
	walk = func(key string) {
		entry := entries[key]
		if entry == nil || seen[key] {
			return
		}
		seen[key] = true
		for _, css := range entry.CSS {
			urls = append(urls, setting.StaticURLPrefix+"/assets/"+css)
		}
		for _, imp := range entry.Imports {
			walk(imp)
		}
	}
	walk(jsEntrySrc)
	return urls
}

// AssetNameFromHashedPath returns the asset entry name for a given hashed asset path.
// Example: returns "theme-gitea-dark" for "css/theme-gitea-dark.CyAaQnn5.css".
// Returns empty string if the path is not found in the manifest.
func AssetNameFromHashedPath(hashedPath string) string {
	return getManifestData().names[hashedPath]
}

// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package public

import (
	"html"
	"html/template"
	"io"
	"path"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"sync/atomic"
	"time"

	"gitea.dev/modules/json"
	"gitea.dev/modules/log"
	"gitea.dev/modules/setting"
)

// https://vite.dev/guide/backend-integration
type manifestEntry struct {
	File    string   `json:"file"`
	Name    string   `json:"name"`
	CSS     []string `json:"css"`
	Imports []string `json:"imports"`
}

type manifestDataStruct struct {
	entries   map[string]*manifestEntry // source path -> entry
	names     map[string]string         // content-hashed output file -> entry name
	modTime   int64
	checkTime time.Time
}

var (
	manifestData atomic.Pointer[manifestDataStruct]
	manifestFS   = sync.OnceValue(AssetFS)
)

const manifestPath = "assets/.vite/manifest.json"

func parseManifest(data []byte) (entries map[string]*manifestEntry, names map[string]string) {
	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &entries); err != nil {
		log.Error("Failed to parse frontend manifest: %v", err)
		return nil, nil
	}
	names = make(map[string]string, len(entries))
	for _, entry := range entries {
		names[entry.File] = entry.Name
	}
	return entries, names
}

func reloadManifest(existingData *manifestDataStruct) *manifestDataStruct {
	now := time.Now()
	data := existingData
	if data != nil && now.Sub(data.checkTime) < time.Second {
		// a single request triggers multiple calls to getHashedPath
		// do not check the manifest file too frequently
		return data
	}

	f, err := manifestFS().Open(manifestPath)
	if err != nil {
		log.Error("Failed to open frontend manifest: %v", err)
		return data
	}
	defer f.Close()

	fi, err := f.Stat()
	if err != nil {
		log.Error("Failed to stat frontend manifest: %v", err)
		return data
	}

	needReload := data == nil || fi.ModTime().UnixNano() != data.modTime
	if !needReload {
		return data
	}

func storeManifestFromBytes(manifestContent []byte, modTime int64, checkTime time.Time) *manifestDataStruct {
	entries, names := parseManifest(manifestContent)
	data := &manifestDataStruct{
		entries:   entries,
		names:     names,
		modTime:   modTime,
		checkTime: checkTime,
	}
	manifestData.Store(data)
	return data
}

func getManifestData() *manifestDataStruct {
	data := manifestData.Load()

	// In production the manifest is immutable (embedded in the binary).
	// In dev mode, check if it changed on disk (for watch-frontend).
	if data == nil || !setting.IsProd {
		data = reloadManifest(data)
	}
	if data == nil {
		data = &manifestDataStruct{}
	}
	return data
}

// devAssetURL returns a source file's Vite dev server URL, panicking in dev/testing if it's absent.
func devAssetURL(src string) string {
	if url := viteDevSourceURL(src); url != "" {
		return url
	}
	setting.PanicInDevOrTesting("Failed to locate source file for asset: %s", src)
	return ""
}

// AssetURI resolves a frontend asset by its source path (the Vite manifest key, e.g.
// "web_src/js/index.ts"). Dev mode serves the source file; production resolves the hashed output.
func AssetURI(srcPath string) string {
	if IsViteDevMode() {
		return devAssetURL(srcPath)
	}
	if entry := getManifestData().entries[srcPath]; entry != nil {
		return setting.StaticURLPrefix + "/assets/" + entry.File
	}
	// The only expected manifest miss is a user's custom theme CSS, served as a static asset
	// under "/assets/css/". Anything else is a misconfigured or missing entry.
	if path.Ext(srcPath) == ".css" {
		return setting.StaticURLPrefix + "/assets/css/" + path.Base(srcPath)
	}
	log.Error("asset not found in frontend manifest: %s", srcPath)
	return setting.StaticURLPrefix + "/assets/" + path.Base(srcPath)
}

// AssetCSSLinks renders the <link> tags for a JS entry's stylesheets: the entry's CSS plus the CSS
// of every statically-imported chunk. Dev links devStylesheetSrc and lets the JS module inject the rest.
func AssetCSSLinks(jsEntrySrc, devStylesheetSrc string) template.HTML {
	var b strings.Builder
	for _, href := range entryStyleURLs(jsEntrySrc, devStylesheetSrc) {
		b.WriteString(`<link rel="stylesheet" href="` + html.EscapeString(href) + `">`)
	}
	return template.HTML(b.String())
}

```bash
mkdir -p /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-everick-Projects-CSCI435-gitea/f5600bd0-6202-47ed-bf8c-ff3037983246/scratchpad && cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-everick-Projects-CSCI435-gitea/f5600bd0-6202-47ed-bf8c-ff3037983246/scratchpad/ramp.mjs <<'EOF'
// Throwaway generator for Gitea theme colour ramps. Not committed.
// Derives the lightness-fraction curve from the stock gitea themes, then
// re-applies that same curve to a new palette's base colour, so a new theme
// keeps the exact visual rhythm of the stock one.
import {readFileSync} from 'node:fs';

const THEMES = 'web_src/css/themes';

export function hex2rgb(hex) {
  const h = hex.replace('#', '');
  return [0, 2, 4].map((i) => parseInt(h.slice(i, i + 2), 16));
}

export function rgb2hsl([r, g, b]) {
  r /= 255; g /= 255; b /= 255;
  const max = Math.max(r, g, b), min = Math.min(r, g, b), d = max - min;
  const l = (max + min) / 2;
  if (d === 0) return [0, 0, l];
  const s = d / (1 - Math.abs(2 * l - 1));
  let h;
  if (max === r) h = ((g - b) / d) % 6;
  else if (max === g) h = (b - r) / d + 2;
  else h = (r - g) / d + 4;
  h *= 60;
  if (h < 0) h += 360;
  return [h, s, l];
}

export function hsl2hex([h, s, l]) {
  const c = (1 - Math.abs(2 * l - 1)) * s;
  const x = c * (1 - Math.abs(((h / 60) % 2) - 1));
  const m = l - c / 2;
  const t = h / 60;
  let rgb;
  if (t < 1) rgb = [c, x, 0];
  else if (t < 2) rgb = [x, c, 0];
  else if (t < 3) rgb = [0, c, x];
  else if (t < 4) rgb = [0, x, c];
  else if (t < 5) rgb = [x, 0, c];
  else rgb = [c, 0, x];
  return '#' + rgb.map((v) => Math.round((v + m) * 255).toString(16).padStart(2, '0')).join('');
}

export const lightnessOf = (hex) => rgb2hsl(hex2rgb(hex))[2];

/** Scale lightness toward 0 (f>0) or toward 1 (g>0), keeping hue and saturation. */
export function scaleL(hex, {toward, amount}) {
  const [h, s, l] = rgb2hsl(hex2rgb(hex));
  const nl = toward === 'black' ? l * (1 - amount) : l + (1 - l) * amount;
  return hsl2hex([h, s, nl]);
}

function readVars(file) {
  const css = readFileSync(`${THEMES}/${file}`, 'utf8');
  const out = {};
  for (const m of css.matchAll(/(--[\w-]+)\s*:\s*(#[0-9a-f]{3,8})\s*;/g)) out[m[1]] = m[2];
  return out;
}

/** Empirically derive the stock fraction curve for one ramp. */
function curve(vars, base, names, toward) {
  const l0 = lightnessOf(vars[base]);
  return names.map((n) => {
    const l = lightnessOf(vars[n]);
    return toward === 'black' ? 1 - l / l0 : (l - l0) / (1 - l0);
  });
}

const seq = (p, kind, n) => Array.from({length: n}, (_, i) => `--color-${p}-${kind}-${i + 1}`);

const light = readVars('theme-gitea-light.css');
const dark = readVars('theme-gitea-dark.css');

// In the light theme, `dark-N` walks toward black and `light-N` toward white.
// The dark theme swaps them, so its `dark-N` is the one walking toward white.
export const CURVES = {
  primary: {
    black: curve(light, '--color-primary', seq('primary', 'dark', 7), 'black'),
    white: curve(light, '--color-primary', seq('primary', 'light', 7), 'white'),
  },
  secondary: {
    black: curve(light, '--color-secondary', seq('secondary', 'dark', 13), 'black'),
    white: curve(light, '--color-secondary', seq('secondary', 'light', 4), 'white'),
  },
  primaryDark: {
    white: curve(dark, '--color-primary', seq('primary', 'dark', 7), 'white'),
    black: curve(dark, '--color-primary', seq('primary', 'light', 7), 'black'),
  },
  secondaryDark: {
    white: curve(dark, '--color-secondary', seq('secondary', 'dark', 13), 'white'),
    black: curve(dark, '--color-secondary', seq('secondary', 'light', 4), 'black'),
  },
};

const ALPHAS = ['19', '33', '4b', '66', '80', '99', 'b3', 'cc', 'e1'];

/**
 * Emit one ramp. `scheme` is 'light' or 'dark'; in a dark theme the dark-N /
 * light-N names are swapped so "dark" always means "more contrast vs the body".
 */
export function ramp(prefix, baseHex, scheme, {contrast} = {}) {
  const isDark = scheme === 'dark';
  const key = prefix === 'primary'
    ? (isDark ? 'primaryDark' : 'primary')
    : (isDark ? 'secondaryDark' : 'secondary');
  const c = CURVES[key];
  const lines = [`  --color-${prefix}: ${baseHex};`];
  if (contrast) lines.push(`  --color-${prefix}-contrast: ${contrast};`);
  // "dark-N" walks toward white in a dark theme, toward black in a light one.
  const darkToward = isDark ? 'white' : 'black';
  const lightToward = isDark ? 'black' : 'white';
  c[darkToward].forEach((amount, i) => {
    lines.push(`  --color-${prefix}-dark-${i + 1}: ${scaleL(baseHex, {toward: darkToward, amount})};`);
  });
  c[lightToward].forEach((amount, i) => {
    lines.push(`  --color-${prefix}-light-${i + 1}: ${scaleL(baseHex, {toward: lightToward, amount})};`);
  });
  ALPHAS.forEach((a, i) => {
    lines.push(`  --color-${prefix}-alpha-${(i + 1) * 10}: ${baseHex}${a};`);
  });
  return lines.join('\n');
}

if (process.argv[2] === '--selftest') {
  // Re-derive the stock ramps from their own base and diff against the file.
  for (const [label, vars, scheme] of [['light', light, 'light'], ['dark', dark, 'dark']]) {
    for (const p of ['primary', 'secondary']) {
      const got = ramp(p, vars[`--color-${p}`], scheme);
      let bad = 0;
      for (const line of got.split('\n')) {
        const [, name, val] = line.match(/(--[\w-]+): (#[0-9a-f]+);/);
        if (vars[name] && vars[name] !== val) { bad++; console.log(`  ${label}/${p} ${name}: file=${vars[name]} gen=${val}`); }
      }
      console.log(`${label}/${p}: ${bad} mismatches`);
    }
  }
}
EOF

# Design: 4 new palettes (12 theme files) for Gitea

## 0. Foundational decision: import-and-override, not standalone

The 100–170 line budget and the 294-variable surface can't both be satisfied by standalone files. Use the same pattern the colorblind variants already use:

```css
@import "./theme-gitea-light.css";   /* or ./theme-gitea-dark.css */

gitea-theme-meta-info { ... }

:root { /* ~120 overrides */ }
```

Why this is safe, verified against the code:

- `parseThemeMetaInfoToMap` uses `strings.LastIndex("gitea-theme-meta-info")`. After Vite inlines the import, the built file is `[base meta][base :root][our meta][our :root]` — ours is last, so ours wins. This is precisely the case covered by the second assertion in `TestParseThemeMetaInfo`.
- `:root` from the import and our local `:root` have equal specificity, so source order decides; ours is later, so ours wins.
- Everything we don't override stays a live `var()` reference and re-resolves against our new values for free (see §2).
- `accent-color: var(--color-accent)` and `color-scheme: light|dark` come from the base and are already correct per-file.

**CSS gotcha:** `@import` must be the first at-rule in the file (before `gitea-theme-meta-info`). The existing files already do this.

---

## 1. Color derivation

### 1a. Primary ramp — I reverse-engineered the exact rule; your "±5% relative HSL steps" reading is close but the endpoints aren't

The 14 primary values in `theme-gitea-light.css` are **Sass `scale-color($base, $lightness: ±p)` with a fixed stop table**, holding HSL hue and saturation constant:

| slot | p |
|---|---|
| dark-1 / light-1 | ∓10% |
| dark-2 / light-2 | ∓20% |
| dark-3 / light-3 | ∓30% |
| dark-4 / light-4 | ∓40% |
| dark-5 / light-5 | ∓60% |
| dark-6 / light-6 | ∓80% |
| dark-7 / light-7 | ∓94% |

with

```
p > 0:  L' = L + (1 - L) * p     (blend toward white)
p < 0:  L' = L * (1 + p)         (blend toward black)
```

I implemented this and it reproduces **all 14 existing hex values from `#4183c4` byte-for-byte**, including `#04080c` and `#f4f8fb`. Your measured "L ≈ 0.206 / 0.102 / 0.031" are exactly `0.5118×0.4`, `×0.2`, `×0.06`.

**Use relative `scale-color`, not absolute L targets.** That is the direct answer to the Solarized-blue-vs-Gruvbox-yellow question: because each step is a fraction of the *remaining headroom*, the ramp degrades gracefully at any base lightness. Verified outputs:

- Solarized `#268bd2` (L=0.49) → dark-7 `#02080d`, light-7 `#f2f8fd` — well spread.
- Gruvbox yellow `#d79921` (L=0.49, but visually light) → dark `#c28a1e … #0d0902`, light `#e0a533 … #fdf9f1` — well spread.
- Nord frost `#88c0d0` (L=0.67) → light-1..4 compress (`#94c6d5 #a0cdd9 #acd3de #b8d9e3`) but stay distinguishable; dark side is fine.
- Catppuccin Mauve `#cba6f7` (L=0.81) → light-1..4 are nearly identical (`#d0aff8 … #e0cafa`). **This is the failure mode.**

**Rule for very light / very dark bases:** if `L(base) > 0.70` or `L(base) < 0.30`, the ramp on the crowded side collapses. Don't patch the algorithm — pick a different base. Concretely: for a *light* theme the primary must be dark enough to be link text, for a *dark* theme light enough. Add a guard to your script: warn if `L < 0.30 || L > 0.70`. Recommended bases below.

### 1b. `--color-primary-contrast`

Pick `#ffffff` vs. the palette's darkest ink by whichever wins WCAG contrast against `--color-primary`. Measured picks:

| primary | white | ink | choose |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nord `#5e81ac` | 4.02 | 4.72 | ink (`#2e3440`) |
| Solarized `#268bd2` | 3.68 | 5.17 | ink (`#002b36`) |
| Gruvbox light `#076678` | 6.60 | 2.88 | `#ffffff` |
| Gruvbox dark `#83a598` | 2.69 | 7.06 | ink (`#282828`) |
| Catppuccin Latte `#1e66f5` | 4.91 | 3.87 | `#ffffff` |
| Catppuccin Mocha `#89b4fa` | 2.10 | 9.03 | ink (`#1e1e2e`) |

Note gitea-light's own `primary-contrast` is only **3.98:1** — so several of these are actually *better* than baseline.

### 1c. Alpha values

Not a computed percentage — a fixed legacy byte table. Copy it verbatim:

```
10→19  20→33  30→4b  40→66  50→80  60→99  70→b3  80→cc  90→e1
```

(`10` and `30` and `90` are not round: `0x19`=9.8%, `0x4b`=29.4%, `0xe1`=88.2%.) Emit `base_hex + byte` for both primary and secondary.

### 1d. Secondary ramp — do NOT reuse the primary algorithm

I measured it; the two base themes use **two different, hand-tuned constructions**:

- **`theme-gitea-light.css`** secondary is a *uniform additive sRGB offset* on all three channels (`-9, -23, -55, -71, -86, -102, … -211`, i.e. −15.6/step from dark-3 onward, clamped at 0), with `light-1..4` additive `+14, +20, +27, +33` where `+33` lands the max channel exactly on `255`. Saturation therefore *rises* as it darkens (S 0.175 → 1.00).
- **`theme-gitea-dark.css`** secondary is multiplicative near the base and lerps toward white at the top; the channel ratios diverge (3.38 / 3.24 / 3.01 at dark-13). Not reproducible by one formula.

Trying to pixel-match either is wasted effort and produces greys that aren't Nord's greys. Instead — and this is the better design anyway — **anchor the secondary ramp on the palette's own neutral scale**, which every one of these four palettes ships:

| palette | light-theme anchors (base → dark-13) | dark-theme anchors (base → dark-13) |
|---|---|---|
| Nord | `#d8dee9` (nord4) → `#2e3440` (nord0) | `#3b4252` (nord1) → `#eceff4` (nord6) |
| Solarized | `#eee8d5` (base2) → `#002b36` (base03) | `#073642` (base02) → `#fdf6e3` (base3) |
| Gruvbox | `#d5c4a1` (bg2) → `#282828` (bg0) | `#3c3836` (bg1) → `#fbf1c7` (fg0) |
| Catppuccin | `#ccd0da` (surface0/Latte) → `#4c4f69` (text/Latte) | `#313244` (surface0/Mocha) → `#cdd6f4` (text/Mocha) |

Algorithm:

```
secondary        = anchorBase
secondary-dark-N = lerp_sRGB(anchorBase, anchorEnd, tDark[N])   N = 1..13
secondary-light-N= lerp_sRGB(anchorBase, anchorNear, tLight[N]) N = 1..4
```

Use the **relative-position tables I measured from the real files** so the perceptual spacing matches Gitea's:

```
// light themes (dark-N walks toward the palette's darkest neutral)
tDark  = [.042, .107, .256, .330, .400, .474, .544, .619, .688, .763, .833, .907, .981]
tLight = [.42, .61, .82, 1.00]            // toward the palette's lightest surface

// dark themes (dark-N walks toward the palette's lightest neutral)
tDark  = [.037, .088, .173, .269, .347, .416, .485, .560, .595, .659, .725, .773, .787]
tLight = [.16, .30, .51, .60]             // toward the palette's darkest neutral
```

These fractions are exactly what gitea-light and gitea-dark use (I derived them from the HSL-L of each stop), so the resulting ramps land in the same visual positions.

### 1e. Script shape (scratchpad, uncommitted)

One file, `~120 lines`, no deps beyond `colord` (already in `node_modules`). Input: a small palette object. Output: the `:root` body ready to paste. Structure:

```
scaleColor(hex, p)            // §1a, HSL, preserve H+S
primaryRamp(base)             // 14 hexes via STEPS = [.10,.20,.30,.40,.60,.80,.94]
alphas(base)                  // 9 hexes via BYTE_TABLE
secondaryRamp(base, end, near, isDark)   // §1d lerp tables
pickContrast(primary, ink)    // §1b
emit(palette)                 // prints the CSS, grouped with the same comment headers
```

Run it once per theme, paste, delete the script. Keep the two lerp tables and the STEPS table as named constants with a one-line comment in the emitted CSS crediting the origin — that's the part a reviewer will want to trust.

---

## 2. Which of the 294 variables to override

I counted the categories in `theme-gitea-light.css`: header/primary/secondary 57, console 9, named 12, named-light 12, named-dark-1 12, named-dark-2 12, ansi 16, series-16 16, other 48, target-based 100 (of which 41 are `--color-syntax-*`).

### Inherit for free — these are already `var()` references

Because we import the base, all of these re-resolve against our new values with **zero lines written**:

```
--color-primary-hover      = var(--color-primary-dark-1)    [light] / light-1 [dark]
--color-primary-active     = var(--color-primary-dark-2)    [light] / light-2 [dark]
--color-secondary-button   = var(--color-secondary-dark-4)
--color-secondary-hover    = var(--color-secondary-dark-5)  [light] / dark-3 [dark]
--color-secondary-active   = var(--color-secondary-dark-6)  [light] / dark-2 [dark]
--color-footer             = var(--color-nav-bg)
--color-input-text         = var(--color-text-dark)
--color-input-border       = var(--color-secondary-dark-1)
--color-nav-hover-bg       = var(--color-secondary-light-1)
--color-nav-text           = var(--color-text)
--color-label-text         = var(--color-text)
--color-placeholder-text   = var(--color-text-light-3)
--color-editor-line-highlight = var(--color-secondary-alpha-30|40)
--color-editor-selection   = var(--color-primary-alpha-30|50)
--color-project-column-bg  = var(--color-secondary-light-4|2)
--color-caret              = var(--color-text-dark|text)
--color-reaction-hover-bg  = var(--color-primary-light-5|4)
--color-reaction-active-bg = var(--color-primary-light-6|5)
--color-accent             = var(--color-primary-light-1)
--color-small-accent       = var(--color-primary-light-6|5)
--color-danger             = var(--color-red)
--color-syntax-link        = var(--color-primary)
--color-ansi-white         = var(--color-console-fg-subtle)
--color-ansi-bright-white  = var(--color-console-fg)
accent-color, color-scheme, --is-dark-theme
```

**That's 24 variables you must not touch.** Overriding any of them with a literal would be a regression.

### Tier 1 — MUST override (≈94 lines). Without these it isn't the palette.

**Primary (26)**
```
--color-primary
--color-primary-contrast
--color-primary-dark-1 … -7        (7)
--color-primary-light-1 … -7       (7)
--color-primary-alpha-10 … -90     (9)
```

**Secondary (27)**
```
--color-secondary
--color-secondary-dark-1 … -13     (13)
--color-secondary-light-1 … -4     (4)
--color-secondary-alpha-10 … -90   (9)
```
Non-negotiable: `--color-secondary` drives every border, input, button, project column, and nav hover. Leaving GitHub's `#d0d7de` next to Nord surfaces is the single most visible mismatch.

**Surfaces + text (23)**
```
--color-body
--color-box-header
--color-box-body
--color-box-body-highlight
--color-text-dark
--color-text
--color-text-light
--color-text-light-1
--color-text-light-2
--color-text-light-3
--color-menu
--color-card
--color-button
--color-code-bg
--color-nav-bg
--color-secondary-nav-bg
--color-input-background
--color-input-toggle-background
--color-secondary-bg
--color-hover-opaque        ← literal; must equal body composited with hover, or hover states flash
--color-shadow-opaque       ← literal
--color-timeline
--color-expand-button
```

**Neutral overlays (6)** — literals tinted `#000017` / `#f3f3f4`. On a warm background (Gruvbox, Solarized light) the cool tint reads as a grey film. Retint to the palette's ink/paper:
```
--color-light
--color-light-border
--color-hover
--color-active
--color-shadow
--color-reaction-bg
```

**Named colors (12)** — cheap, and the signature of every one of these palettes (Nord red `#bf616a` vs Gruvbox red `#cc241d`):
```
--color-red --color-orange --color-yellow --color-olive --color-green
--color-teal --color-blue --color-violet --color-purple --color-pink
--color-brown --color-black
```

### Tier 2 — strongly recommended (≈25 lines)

**Status (12)** — skip `priority-*`, which is rarely surfaced:
```
--color-error-border/-bg/-bg-active/-bg-hover/-text   (5)
--color-success-border/-bg/-text                      (3)
--color-warning-border/-bg/-text                      (3)
--color-info-border/-bg/-text                         (3)
```
Actually 14 including all of error's four bg states; trim `-bg-active`/`-bg-hover` to hit 12 if budget is tight.

**Diff (13)** — a git forge's most-looked-at surface; the stock greens/reds will clash badly with Gruvbox or Solarized backgrounds:
```
--color-diff-added-fg/-linenum-bg/-row-bg/-row-border/-word-bg
--color-diff-moved-row-bg/-row-border
--color-diff-removed-fg/-linenum-bg/-row-bg/-row-border/-word-bg
--color-diff-inactive
```

### Tier 3 — optional (25 lines), high value for *these specific* palettes

```
--color-console-fg/-fg-subtle/-bg/-border/-hover-bg/-active-bg/-menu-bg/-menu-border/-link  (9)
--color-ansi-{black,red,green,yellow,blue,magenta,cyan} + 7 bright     (14, the 2 `white` ones inherit)
```
Solarized and Gruvbox users overwhelmingly want these — the ANSI 16 is the *reason* those palettes exist. Include them for Solarized/Gruvbox; optional for Nord/Catppuccin.

### Explicitly leave inherited

| category | count | why |
|---|---|---|
| `--color-series-16-*` | 16 | **Identical in both base themes** — upstream treats them as theme-independent chart colors. Overriding fights the base's categorical-distinctness tuning. |
| `--color-*-badge*` | 12 | `1a` / `4d` alpha over whatever background; reads fine on any palette. |
| `--color-syntax-*` | 41 | The base pair is already contrast-tuned per scheme. Retinting 41 vars is where a palette theme goes from "reviewable" to "unreviewable", and a bad syntax set is worse than a neutral one. Ship v1 without; add later as a separate PR if wanted. |
| `--color-{name}-light`, `-dark-1`, `-dark-2` | 36 | Low value-per-line. They're hover/active shades of the named colors; a small hue drift between `--color-red` and `--color-red-dark-1` is barely perceptible. If you want them, `color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-red), white 25%)` gets you all 36 in 36 self-documenting lines — but check `color-mix` browser-baseline policy first. |
| `--color-markup-*`, `--color-tooltip-*`, `--color-label-*`, `--color-highlight-*`, `--color-transparency-grid-*`, `--color-overlay-backdrop`, `--color-workflow-edge-hover`, `--color-git`, `--color-logo`, `--color-grey*`, `--color-gold`, `--color-white` | ~18 | Brand-fixed or low-visibility. |

### Line budget

```
@import + blank                     2
gitea-theme-meta-info block         5
:root { / --is-dark-theme (restated for the reader)  2
Tier 1                             94
Tier 2                             25
section comments + blanks          ~10
}                                   1
------------------------------------
                                  ~139  (~164 with Tier 3)
```

Lands inside your 100–170 target. Keep the base file's section comment headers (`/* named colors */` etc.) so a reviewer can diff sections side-by-side against `theme-gitea-light.css`.

## 3. Contrast verification

**The critical finding: an absolute WCAG gate is unusable, because the stock themes already fail it.** I ran the check — here are real numbers from `theme-gitea-light.css`:

```
FAIL  4.23 (>=4.5)  --color-text-light-3 on --color-body
FAIL  3.98 (>=4.5)  --color-primary on --color-body
FAIL  3.98 (>=4.5)  --color-primary-contrast on --color-primary
FAIL  1.58 (>=3)    --color-secondary-dark-1 on --color-body
FAIL  3.72 (>=4.5)  --color-ansi-blue on --color-console-bg
```
and from `theme-gitea-dark.css`:
```
FAIL  4.45 (>=4.5)  --color-text-light-3 on --color-body
FAIL  4.14 (>=4.5)  --color-primary on --color-body
FAIL  3.98 (>=4.5)  --color-primary-contrast on --color-primary
FAIL  4.49 (>=4.5)  --color-error-text on --color-error-bg
FAIL  1.82 (>=3)    --color-secondary-dark-1 on --color-body
```

### Proposed check: baseline-delta, not pass/fail

A ~60-line scratchpad script. Dependencies already installed: `postcss` and `colord` + `colord/plugins/a11y` (import path is `colord/plugins/a11y`, **not** `.../a11y.mjs` — the `.mjs` subpath isn't in the package `exports` and will throw `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`; I hit this).

```
1. postcss.parse(file) → collect every :root decl starting with "--"
   (parse base file first, then the palette file on top — models the import)
2. resolve var(--x) references iteratively (max 10 hops)
3. flatten(fg, bg): colord(fg).alpha() < 1 → colord(bg).mix(colord(fg).alpha(1), alpha)
   ← required; colord's .contrast() ignores alpha, and ~8 of these vars are 8-digit hex
4. for each pair: ratio = flatten(fg,bg).contrast(colord(bg))
5. compare against the SAME pair measured on theme-gitea-light/dark
   → report REGRESSION only when ratio < baseline AND ratio < threshold
   → report IMPROVED when it crosses the threshold the base was failing
```

Pair list (fg, bg, threshold):

```
4.5:1 body text
  text / body            text / box-body        text / box-header
  text / menu            text / card            text / button
  text-light-1 / body    text-light-2 / body    text-light-3 / body
  nav-text / nav-bg
  primary / body                       ← link text
  primary-contrast / primary           ← button label
  primary-contrast / primary-hover     ← button hover label
  error-text / error-bg       success-text / success-bg
  warning-text / warning-bg   info-text / info-bg
  diff-added-fg / diff-added-row-bg    diff-removed-fg / diff-removed-row-bg
  text / diff-added-row-bg             text / diff-removed-row-bg
  text / diff-added-word-bg            text / diff-removed-word-bg   ← commonly missed
  console-fg / console-bg
  ansi-{black..bright-white} / console-bg        ← 16 pairs; Solarized's classic trap
3:1 UI
  secondary-dark-1 / input-background   ← input border
  accent / body                         ← focus ring
  primary / body
  timeline / body
```

Output a table per theme with `Δ vs baseline`. Any negative Δ on a pair the base passes is a blocker; everything else is informational. This is the cheap, non-bikesheddable version — it can't be argued with, because it's measured against shipped Gitea.

Already-measured signals to act on:
- `nord10 #5e81ac` on `nord6 #eceff4` = **3.49**, below gitea-light's 3.98 → for `nord-light`, use `scale-color(#5e81ac, -10%)`-ish (`≈#52719a`) as the primary instead, or take `nord6` down to a whiter body.
- `#268bd2` on Solarized `base3 #fdf6e3` = **3.41** → same treatment.
- Gruvbox light `#076678` on `#fbf1c7` = **5.81**, Catppuccin Latte `#1e66f5` on `#eff1f5` = **4.34**, Nord dark `#88c0d0` on `#2e3440` = **6.24**, Catppuccin Mocha `#89b4fa` on `#1e1e2e` = **7.78** — all fine.
